guide.summary: Custom OAuth 2.0 app for customer enterprises (self-serve); Server app (JWT or CCG) in customer enterprise (self-serve); Listed in Box Integrations gallery (app review).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Custom OAuth 2.0 app for customer enterprises (self-serve). Hardest: Listed in Box Integrations gallery (app review).

composio.note: Composio manages OAuth2 for Box, so prototypes need no own app. A separate Box MCP toolkit exists and needs your own OAuth app.

need_own_app.answer: Not for prototypes, since Composio's managed Box app works. For launch you likely want your own app so consent shows your brand, you get dedicated quota, and you control scopes.
reasons: Consent screen shows Composio's name with the managed app
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users
Composio's default scopes may not cover what you need
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum trigger polling interval

prerequisites.title: Box developer account
prerequisites.detail: A free developer account gives access to the Developer Console. Enterprise accounts can also use it.

prerequisites.title: Multi-factor authentication on your Box account
prerequisites.detail: MFA must be enabled to view a client secret or generate a keypair.

prerequisites.title: Pick the right app type first
prerequisites.detail: A User app cannot be converted to a Server app or the reverse; you must create a new app.

steps.title: Create the app in Developer Console
steps.detail: Log in, select New App, choose User for OAuth 2.0 (or Server for JWT/CCG), and create it.
steps.done_when: The app opens on its Configuration tab.

steps.title: Draft the minimal scope list
steps.detail: List only the permissions the agent needs and the access level. Add scopes before admin authorization.
steps.done_when: A scope list is ready to enter.

steps.title: Set scopes and redirect URI
steps.detail: Enter scopes. Paste the redirect URI copied from the Composio dashboard into the OAuth 2.0 Redirect URI section; it must match exactly.
steps.done_when: The redirect URI is saved on the Configuration tab.

steps.title: Copy client ID and secret
steps.detail: Copy them from App Details on the Configuration tab.
steps.done_when: You have the client ID and secret.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Through Composio's API, create a Box auth config using your own client ID and secret.
steps.done_when: The auth config exists in Composio.

steps.title: Send client ID to customer admin
steps.detail: Give the customer's Box Admin your Client ID; they authorize or enable the app in Admin Console, Platform Apps.

steps.title: Wait for admin decision
steps.detail: The developer gets an email when the admin approves or declines.

steps.title: Submit to Box Integrations
steps.detail: Submit the production-ready OAuth 2.0 app in the Developer Console and follow the Box Integrations checklist.

steps.title: Wait for partner review
steps.detail: Box reviews the submission; the duration is undocumented.

traps.title: A newly created enterprise can authorize up to 10,000
traps.detail: A newly created enterprise can authorize up to 10,000 custom apps.

traps.title: A developer token generated in the Developer Console has
traps.detail: A developer token generated in the Developer Console has the same 60-minute lifetime as other access tokens and is meant for development only.

traps.title: Server apps cannot skip admin authorization
traps.detail: Calls before authorization return unauthorized_client. Box staff say there is no workaround.

traps.title: Admin may never respond
traps.detail: One developer's request stayed pending for about two months and the app ended up disabled.

traps.title: Scope changes break authorization
traps.detail: Changed scopes need re-authorization to take effect. Enterprise developers must resubmit to an admin.

traps.title: Redirect URI must match exactly
traps.detail: Box does exact matching and rejects duplicates. With several URIs, a missing redirect_uri parameter causes a redirect_uri_missing error.

traps.title: Custom apps count toward customer API quota
traps.detail: Custom app calls count toward the enterprise's monthly allocation; partner integrations do not.

blockers.symptom: unauthorized_client: This app is not authorized by the enterprise
blockers.what_it_means: The Server app is not yet authorized in that enterprise.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the customer's Box Admin to authorize it in Admin Console, Platform Apps, using your Client ID.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the admin request email with the Client ID and scope list.

blockers.what_it_means: The customer admin has not acted on the request.
blockers.what_to_do: Follow up with the admin and find an internal sponsor at the customer.
